title: Present Simple
tagline: habits, facts and routines: I work, she works
why: We use the present simple to talk about our lives: jobs, routines, likes and facts. It is the tense you use most when you meet people, so small mistakes like he work are easy to hear.
able: describe your daily routine and your job
ask and answer questions like Where do you live? and What does your partner do?
talk about timetables: The train leaves at 8:15.
mistakes: I go always to bed late.
use: habits and routines: I walk the dog every morning.
facts that are always true: Water freezes at 0 degrees.
jobs and long-term situations: My sister works for the city.
form: I / you / we / they work. He / she / it works.
Do you work? Does he work? Where does she work?
signals: always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never, every day, on Mondays, once a week, twice a year, in the morning
tip: Only one -s in a sentence: She works, but Does she work? and She doesn't work. Frequency words go before the main verb but after be: I often cook. I'm often late.

pick.q: My brother ___ in a hospital in Hamilton.
pick.why: My brother = he, so add -s: works. 'Is work' mixes two tenses.
Your parents = they, so use Do: Do your parents live near you?
With she, use doesn't + the base verb: doesn't eat. No -s after doesn't.

pick.q: The museum ___ at 10 a.m. on Sundays.
pick.why: Timetables use the present simple. The museum = it, so opens.
Questions need do or does before the subject: How often do you go?

pick.q: My daughter ___ her homework after dinner.
pick.why: Frequency words go before the main verb, and my daughter = she, so: usually does.

pick.q: The sun always ___ in the west.
pick.why: A fact that is always true uses the present simple. The sun = it, so sets.
Your husband = he, so use does. The main verb do stays without -s.

type.q: My neighbour ___ (wash) his car every Sunday.
type.why: Verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x or -o add -es: washes.

type.q: She ___ (study) English three evenings a week.
type.why: Consonant + y: change the y to -ies. study becomes studies.

type.q: We ___ (not / have) a car. We take the subway.
type.why: With we, use don't + the base verb: don't have.
Your sister = she, so: does your sister work? The -s goes on does, not on work.

type.q: He ___ (not / like) cold weather, so he goes to Florida every winter.
type.why: With he, use doesn't + the base verb: doesn't like (not doesn't likes).

type.q: The train to Ottawa ___ (leave) at 6:45 every morning.
type.why: Timetables use the present simple. The train = it, so leaves.
Vowel + y just adds -s: plays (not plaies).
A question with you: do + you + base verb. Do you speak French?

spot.q: My father drive to work every day.
spot.why: My father = he, so add -s: My father drives to work every day.
After does, use the base verb with no -s: Does your boss speak Spanish?
They takes don't, not doesn't: They don't eat breakfast.

spot.q: I am walk to work every day.
spot.why: A daily habit uses the present simple, with no am: I walk to work every day.

spot.q: She watchs the news every night.
spot.why: Verbs ending in -ch add -es: She watches the news every night.

order.a: How often do you visit your parents?
order.why: Question word + do + subject + base verb: How often do you visit your parents?

order.a: My sister never drinks coffee in the evening.
alt: In the evening my sister never drinks coffee.
order.why: Never goes before the main verb, and my sister = she, so drinks.

order.a: What time does the store close on Sundays?
order.why: What time + does + the store + base verb close. No -s on close after does.

order.a: He doesn't usually work on weekends.
alt: He usually doesn't work on weekends.
Usually he doesn't work on weekends.
order.why: Doesn't + base verb work. Usually can go before or after doesn't.

pick.q: My kids ___ to school by bus.
pick.why: My kids = they, so no -s: go.
This train = it, so use Does + base verb: Does this train go to Montreal?
Frequency words go after be: I am never late. 'I never late' has no verb.
Our office = it, so add -es: closes.

pick.q: He ___ to the radio in the car.
pick.why: Always goes before the main verb, and he needs -s: always listens.
Questions need do before the subject, and you takes do: Why do you study English?

type.q: My mother ___ (fix) everything in the house.
He ___ (fly) to Calgary twice a month for work.
type.why: Consonant + y: change the y to -ies. fly becomes flies.

type.q: I ___ (not / understand) this email. Can you help me?
type.why: With I, use don't + the base verb: I don't understand.
The bank = it, so use does + base verb: What time does the bank open?
Go adds -es after he, she, it: goes.
With it, use doesn't + the base verb: It doesn't snow much.
A coffee = it, so use does + base verb: How much does a coffee cost?
Have is irregular: he, she, it has. Our teacher has two cats.

spot.why: After does, use the base verb with no -s: Where does she live?

spot.q: My boss don't answer emails on Fridays.
spot.why: My boss = he or she, so use doesn't: My boss doesn't answer emails on Fridays.

spot.q: I drink always tea in the morning.
spot.why: Always goes before the main verb: I always drink tea in the morning.

spot.q: He trys to call his mother every day.
spot.why: Consonant + y: change the y to -ies. He tries to call his mother.

order.a: Where does your brother live now?
order.why: Where + does + your brother + base verb live. No -s on live after does.

order.a: We sometimes eat dinner in front of the TV.
alt: Sometimes we eat dinner in front of the TV.
We eat dinner in front of the TV sometimes.
order.why: Sometimes can go before the main verb or at the start: We sometimes eat dinner...

order.a: The movie starts at eight tonight.
alt: Tonight the movie starts at eight.
The movie starts tonight at eight.
order.why: A schedule uses the present simple. The movie = it, so starts.

bank.q: My uncle ___ a small restaurant in Montreal.
bank.why: My uncle = he, so owns. Own is a state verb, so we don't say is owning.
With you, use Do + base verb: Do you like spicy food?

bank.q: The children ___ TV on school nights.
bank.why: The children = they, so don't + base verb: don't watch.

bank.q: She ___ the dishes after every meal.
bank.why: She needs -s, and verbs ending in -sh add -es: washes.
Questions need does before he, then the base verb: How does he get to work?
A timetable uses the present simple. The ferry = it, so leaves.

bank.q: My grandparents ___ for a walk after lunch.
bank.why: Often goes before the main verb, and grandparents = they, so go with no -s.
A fact that is always true uses the present simple. Ice = it, so melts.
Verbs ending in -ch add -es after he or she: teaches.
With we, use don't + the base verb: We don't work on holidays.
Your daughter = she, so use does + base verb: What sports does your daughter play?

bank.q: The baby ___ (cry) when she is hungry.
bank.why: Consonant + y: change the y to -ies. The baby cries.
With he, use doesn't + the base verb: He doesn't drink alcohol.
She takes does: Does she work from home?

bank.q: My son go to bed at nine.
bank.why: My son = he, so add -es: My son goes to bed at nine.

bank.q: The library closes early on Fridays.
bank.why: Correct! The library = it, so closes.

bank.q: I don't know what this word means.
bank.why: Correct! This word = it, so means takes -s. There is no do or does before it.

bank.a: What do you usually do on Saturday mornings?
bank.why: What + do + you + usually + base verb do. Usually goes before the main verb.

bank.a: My husband doesn't cook very often.
bank.why: Doesn't + base verb cook. Very often goes at the end.

bank.a: Does this store accept credit cards?
bank.why: Does + this store + base verb accept. No -s on accept after does.
